deduplication: Canonical source URLs; language and tracking query parameters are normalized when they identify the same document.

sources.title: Cabinet approves the IndiaAI Mission
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
sources.caveat: An authorization and programme-design source, not evidence that the target capacity was delivered.

sources.title: With robust and high-end common computing facility in place, India all set to launch its own AI model
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
sources.caveat: The release describes roughly 10,000 GPUs at the initial stage and 8,693 more to be added; it does not establish that the remainder was then live.

sources.title: India’s Common Compute Capacity Crosses 34,000 GPUs
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
sources.caveat: The release says 34,333 GPUs and distinguishes empanelled from additional capacity, but does not define installed, live, or consumed capacity.

sources.title: Government supporting organisations and consortia to develop sovereign foundational models
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
sources.caveat: Reports 38,231 GPUs onboarded from 14 empanelled providers and an average rate near ₹65 per GPU-hour except selected high-end GPUs; retain the release’s own wording.

sources.title: Data centre capacity in the country has increased from about 375 MW in 2020 to around 1,500 MW by 2025
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
sources.caveat: This release labels 13.56 GW as projected data-centre electricity demand by 2031–32; the 30 March 2026 Rajya Sabha answer labels the same figure projected data-centre capacity. The official descriptions conflict.

sources.title: Semiconductor and AI Revolution
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
sources.caveat: Reports 45,000+ shared GPUs as of June 2026 and 237 projects with 93.18 lakh GPU-hours by August 2026; it does not define the GPU-hours as consumed, allocated, or another metering state.

sources.title: IndiaAI Compute Portal: eligibility criteria
sources.caveat: A live programme page; eligibility and review criteria should be rechecked before being treated as current.

sources.title: IndiaAI Compute Portal
sources.caveat: Describes application, approval, provider and allocation processes; the capture is not a dated utilisation ledger.

sources.title: IndiaAI Compute Portal price calculator
sources.caveat: Lists accelerator-specific rates and reservation periods but gives no capture date or general subsidy rule; not directly comparable with the PIB average rate.

sources.title: Data Centres Power and Water Infrastructure Crisis, Rajya Sabha Unstarred Question No. 4151
sources.caveat: The answer gives a national generation-adequacy statement and sector capacity projections; these do not measure local grid connection availability or data-centre electricity draw.

sources.title: Land, water, and energy footprint of India’s data centres
sources.publisher: Council on Energy, Environment and Water
sources.caveat: The cited 2024 electricity and water estimates rely on underlying third-party sources; they are not a government meter-based inventory.

sources.title: India data centre 2026 mid-year report
sources.caveat: An industry market estimate; distinguish delivered stock, absorption, pre-commitments and future pipeline.

sources.title: India’s data centre pipeline reaches 8.33 GW on AI and cloud demand surge
sources.publisher: The Hindu BusinessLine, reporting Knight Frank India
sources.caveat: Separates 1.6 GW live, 0.32 GW under construction, 2.92 GW committed and 5.41 GW early-stage; those components total 8.65 GW, not the article's 8.33 GW headline, and the latter stages are not operating capacity.

sources.title: India Data Centre Market Update 2025
sources.caveat: Period is 2025 year-end; the report distinguishes under-construction projects from committed and early-stage pipeline.

sources.title: IndiaAI Mission likely to rewire after GPU glitch
sources.caveat: Reports access to about 30,000 GPUs against a 45,000 commitment and possible recalibration; these are reported terms, not a government-reconciled inventory.

sources.title: AI models developed under IndiaAI Mission represent important progress in building India’s own AI capabilities
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
sources.caveat: Government programme-output claims; they do not independently establish model quality, adoption, or public-service impact.

sources.title: India’s Data Centre Market in a New Era
sources.caveat: Estimates roughly 1,530 MW of operational stock in January–September 2025 but does not define operational capacity in the captured text.

sources.title: India’s power-hungry data centre sector at a crossroads
sources.publisher: Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis
sources.caveat: Independent analysis with current and projected values; cite estimates and recommendations as IEEFA’s, not as measured official totals.

sources.title: Government response on data-centre water consumption and cooling
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
sources.caveat: The statement that no concerns were received is not equivalent to a measured national water-use inventory.
